newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia Zoo to rebuild burned primate house.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia Zoo to rebuild burned primate house.

text.p: The Philadelphia Zoo unveiled plans Tuesday to build a new primate centre to replace a facility that burned in December 1995 and killed 23 prize animals.

Groundbreaking for the $21 million facility was scheduled for the fall of 1997, and completion targeted for 1999, officials said. Efforts were continuing to raise the final $5 million to build the centre.
Dr Andrew Baker, curator of primates at the zoo, said the centre would house gorillas, orangatangs, gibbons, and several species of smaller and medium-sized primates.
The fire was described as the worst disaster in the history of American zoos.
